questions.prompt: What is a composable in Vue?

options.text: A function (named useX) that uses the Composition API to encapsulate and reuse stateful logic
A special kind of component tag

questions.explanation: A composable is a reusable function, conventionally named useX, that packages reactive state and behavior using the Composition API.

questions.prompt: Two components call the same composable that declares its state inside the function. Do they share that state?

options.text: No — each call creates its own independent state

questions.explanation: State created inside the composable is per-call. To share one instance across the app, declare the state at module scope (outside the function).

questions.prompt: How does a composable make components share a single state instance?

options.text: By declaring the reactive state at module scope, outside the function

questions.explanation: Module-scoped state (declared outside the useX function) is created once and shared by every caller — a lightweight store pattern.

questions.prompt: By convention, a composable's name starts with the word ______. (one word)
questions.explanation: Composables are named useX (useMouse, useFetch, useCounter) by convention.

questions.prompt: Why did composables replace mixins? Select all that apply.

options.text: With mixins it was unclear which mixin a property came from
Composables make the source of each value explicit and renamable
Mixins only work on the server

questions.explanation: Composables avoid mixins' name collisions and unclear origins; you see the imports and returned names and can rename on destructure. Mixins are not server-only.

questions.prompt: Where should a composable put its event-listener cleanup?

options.text: Nowhere — Vue never cleans up listeners
In an onUnmounted hook inside the composable, so it runs for the calling component

questions.explanation: A composable registers onUnmounted internally; the hook belongs to whichever component called it, so cleanup happens automatically on unmount.
